title: Tango in Barcelona and joining Marcelino Guerra
summary: The Barcelona tango band did not influence him; he first subbed with Marcelino Guerra's band around 1945.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: I see. All right, well let's get into this Latin music. How did you ever -- did your experience in Barcelona have anything to do with you getting into Latin music?
Oh, no. Barcelona was there, we were just doing our regular thing. You know.
You heard a tango band there?

I heard, I liked tango music, because I thought [Canaro] had -- course for the first time hearing a tango band I thought it was very beautiful music, but I never thought -- it never influenced me one way or the other.

But, the band I worked with here, was Marcelino Guerrero, I was just going up as a substitute, you know, and I didn't care too much about it at all. Because the band was a great band, but it didn't -- move me.
This was in the '40's, in what, '46, '7?
It was around '45, around that time.
It was around the time when Dizzy started doing a lot of things?
